name: Project Alpha
description: A fully fleshed-out example: live site, full pageContent mix, and every block variant represented.

pageContent.text: Project Alpha started as a **weekend experiment** and grew into a full internal tool. The goal was simple: replace a spreadsheet-based workflow with something the whole team could actually use.
The dashboard view was the first thing built, since it's what most users see *every single day*. Keeping it fast mattered more than keeping it flashy.
Two views of the reporting module — the summary card layout on the left, and the detailed drill-down on the right. Both pull from the same underlying query, just formatted differently.
Check out the [live demo](https://example.com) if you want to poke around yourself. Source is also public, linked above.

name: Project Beta
description: No live site — this slug page is the only place to see it. Each paragraph pairs with exactly one image.

pageContent.text: Project Beta is a hardware companion app with no public deployment, so this page carries the full weight of showing what it does.
The pairing flow took a few iterations to get right — early versions required a manual device ID entry, which nobody wants to type on a phone.

name: Project Gamma
description: An example of the fallback path — no pageContent at all, so the slug page falls back to the legacy image gallery grid.

name: Project Delta
description: A text-heavy writeup with no images anywhere in pageContent — good for testing the block-text-only layout.

pageContent.text: Project Delta doesn't have much to look at — it's a CLI tool, so screenshots wouldn't add much. What it *does* have is a genuinely interesting build process worth writing about.
The trickiest part was handling **cross-platform path resolution** without pulling in a heavy dependency just for that one problem.
If you want to see it in action, the [README](https://github.com/placeholder) has a full walkthrough with example output.

name: Project Epsilon
description: Opens with a plain paragraph, then a two-image staggered block — useful for checking the stagger/flip layout in isolation.

pageContent.text: Project Epsilon is a small internal analytics view. Nothing fancy under the hood, but the UI went through a lot of revisions.
Before and after the redesign — same data, very different first impression.

name: Project Zeta
description: The bare-minimum entry — no pageContent, no images. Good edge case for confirming nothing crashes when both are empty.
